description: "To ensure the next generation is equipped to lead in the AI era, Google's Economic and Community Development programme and WeThinkCode has committed to build a R3 million digital innovation centre at the George Tabor Campus of South West Gauteng TVET College in Soweto. Once complete, the centre will serve as a scalable skills platform built to reach talent the industry usually overlooks."

recipient: Cenfri NPC (Cape Town, South Africa; region served Africa)
title: Cenfri NPC Grant
description: "To equip central banks and financial services providers with a tool that identifies financial arbitrage transactions to improve the measurement of Digital Merchant Payments and the accuracy of credit scores in the market." Duration 36 months; grant topic "Inclusive Financial Systems"; division Global Growth & Opportunity.

title: Quona Capital — Jem Series A, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> South African HR technology company Jem has raised $8.4 million in a Series A funding round led by global fintech investor Quona Capital, as it expands its workforce management platform for frontline workers.
>
> The Cape Town-based company says the funding will support the development of additional products and features, including time and attendance, rostering, onboarding, employee assistance programmes and credit scores.
>
> The Series A round also included University Tech Fund, E4E and angel investors, including former Old Mutual CEO Iain Williamson.

title: AlphaCode Venture Partners — Moment Series A, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Moment, a pan-African fintech, announced the close of its $22 million Series A funding round, led by AlphaCode Venture Partners, with continued investment from General Catalyst, MultiChoice, and fresh investment from Canal+. Since inception, Moment has raised $55 million to develop one of the Continent's most advanced payment infrastructure businesses, offering a comprehensive suite of payment collection and revenue retention solutions to corporate and enterprise merchants. The company will use the additional funding from this Series A round to deepen its network, enhance its platform and accelerate expansion across Africa.

title: Scaling up DIME
description: Scaling Up DIME strengthens digital and financial infrastructure for township MSMEs in South Africa, with a focus on youth- and women-led enterprises. The project improves enterprise visibility, digital onboarding, finance readiness, alternative credit assessment, and access to inclusive market and financing pathways. By scaling DIME as a township enterprise digital and data backbone, the project supports more resilient, finance-ready, and digitally enabled township economies.

title: Pepkor — Shop2Shop/Flash merger into FintechCo, 2026
description: "Retail giant Pepkor has merged Flash, its wholly-owned fintech subsidiary, with Shop2Shop to create merchant commerce and fintech platform FintechCo, with annual throughput exceeding R200 billion." "Pepkor will acquire a controlling 57.1% interest in FintechCo through a combination of a R1.57 billion cash subscription for new shares in Shop2Shop and the contribution of its entire 100% shareholding in Flash, which has been valued at R10.6 billion." "The proposed transaction is subject to various conditions precedent, which include, but are not limited to, receiving all necessary regulatory and competition authority approvals." Pepkor states an ambition "to build a leading digital bank with a nationwide distribution footprint" and plans "a planned future listing of FintechCo".

title: Equinix — South Africa data centre expansion, 2026
description: "Global data centre operator Equinix Inc. is expanding in South Africa with a planned $438 million investment, as it seeks to tap into growing demand for artificial intelligence and cloud services across Africa." "The company... said it will build additional facilities in Johannesburg and Cape Town." "Sandile Dube, Equinix's managing director for South Africa, said the company has secured about 327,000 square metres of land for future development. The expansion is expected to add roughly 160 megawatts of data centre capacity." "All investments are funded by our own balance sheet." Per the companion report, Equinix "has bought more land in that city and also in Cape Town, totalling R890 million."

title: Vodacom — Mpumalanga network capital expenditure, 2026
description: "Vodacom Mpumalanga has reinforced its commitment to connecting communities and advancing digital inclusion through a significant investment of over R600 million in network infrastructure and technology this financial year to expand broadband connectivity and support growing demand for digital services across Mpumalanga." "The investment is focused on expanding network coverage, enhancing connectivity, improving network resilience and capacity, and extending access to digital services in underserved rural, township and urban areas of the province." "The rollout will target all 17 local municipalities across Mpumalanga, spanning the Ehlanzeni, Gert Sibande and Nkangala district municipalities."

title: Vodacom — KwaZulu-Natal network capital expenditure, 2026
description: "Today, Vodacom KwaZulu-Natal announced a strategic investment of R1 billion in network infrastructure for the 2027 financial year." "A significant portion of the investment, approximately R419 million, will be directed towards radio network expansion and modernisation. This includes new site builds, LTE and 5G upgrades, coverage expansion, and capacity improvements" … "Vodacom will also invest more than R173 million in transmission infrastructure, including fibre and microwave network upgrades." "The region has set aside R63.5 million towards an energy resilience programme".

title: Vodacom — Western Cape network capital expenditure, 2026
description: "Vodacom Western Cape is making bold strides towards digital inclusion through an investment of more than R500 million in network infrastructure during the current financial year." "The largest portion of the capital expenditure budget, approximately R380 million, will be allocated to Radio Access Network (RAN) modernisation. More than 50 sites across the province will be upgraded or replaced with next-generation cellular infrastructure" … "In addition, more than 50 sites will receive 4G capacity upgrades using the 700MHz spectrum." "The remaining investment will be directed towards energy resilience projects".

title: MTN — South Africa ICT infrastructure investment, 2026
description: "Telecommunications operator MTN has pledged to invest 21.8 billion South African rand (US$1.3 billion) over the next three years to expand ICT infrastructure and advance the digital economy in South Africa." "The announcement was made at the annual South Africa Investment Conference in Sandton, Johannesburg, this week." "By the end of 2028, it expects to invest a total of almost R22 billion ($1.3 billion) in the country." MTN SA spent R6.8 billion ($404 million) on its network in 2025.

title: Oakvale Invest — Tennsa, 2026
description: "South African startup Tennsa, an AI business intelligence platform built for SMEs, has become the first portfolio company of Oakvale Invest, Africa's first AI-focused pre-seed fund." "The startup has now become the first investment of Oakvale Invest, which has invested more than ZAR1 million (US$61,000) in the company."

title: Telkom — Telkom AI Institute (South Africa), 2026
description: "Telkom pledges USD 6.1 million to establish the Telkom AI Institute, a platform designed to equip South Africans with AI and digital skills, foster innovation, and accelerate inclusive participation in the digital economy." The pledge was one of several announced as ITU's Partner2Connect Digital Coalition surpassed US$100 billion in commitments at the WSIS Forum 2026 in Geneva.

recipient: Naked Insurance (Naked Financial Technology Pty Ltd)
title: DEG Equity Investment in Naked Insurtech South Africa Series B2 (2025)
description: DEG provides USD 4 million in equity capital to South African insurtech Naked Insurance as part of its USD 38 million Series B2 funding round. The round is led by global impact investor BlueOrchard with continued support from Hollard Insurance, Yellowwoods, IFC, and DEG. recipient: Open Access Data Centres (OADC), a WIOCC subsidiary
title: Ninety One — Open Access Data Centres local-currency loan for a new South African data centre, 2025
description:
Verbatim from the release:

> Ninety One also committed $15 million in local currency to Open Access Data Centres (OADC), a WIOCC subsidiary, to construct a new data centre in South Africa and expand existing facilities.

> The funding forms part of a total $65 million debt raise which includes a $20 million commitment from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and $15 million from Proparco.

> All financing arrangements, including EAAIF’s $15 million senior secured loan facility, have a 10-year tenor and are structured as sustainability-linked facilities. The cost of the financing is directly tied to WIOCC achieving ambitious sustainability-linked targets, ensuring that its digital expansion is also sustainable. Key performance indicators include EDGE certification for new data centres – a global standard for resource-efficient and zero-carbon buildings – and Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) targets for operating facilities.

title: Microsoft Azure South Africa — ZAR 5.4B AI and Cloud Expansion 2025-2027
description: Microsoft announced ZAR 5.4 billion (approximately USD 295 million) to expand cloud and AI infrastructure in South Africa by end of 2027, announced by President Brad Smith on March 6, 2025 alongside President Cyril Ramaphosa. Includes construction of a second cloud infrastructure region in Centurion, expanded data centre capacity, power and water readiness, and AI skills development for government and private sector. Builds on the ZAR 20.4bn Microsoft states it invested over the preceding three years, held as 2025-03-06-microsoft-zaf-azure-microsoft-south-africa-datacentres-zar-204bn.

title: Microsoft Azure South Africa — ZAR 20.4bn spent on the first enterprise datacentres (disclosed 2025)
description: At an event in Johannesburg on 6 March 2025, Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith announced a further ZAR 5.4 billion of cloud and AI infrastructure spending in South Africa by the end of 2027, and in doing so disclosed that this "builds on the company's ZAR 20.4 billion investment over the past three years to establish the nation's first enterprise-grade datacentres in Johannesburg and Cape Town". Moneyweb reported it as the first time Microsoft had publicly stated its South African datacentre investment, and put the combined figure at ZAR 25.8 billion. The Azure South Africa North (Johannesburg) and South Africa West (Cape Town) regions opened in March 2019 — the first enterprise-grade cloud datacentre regions on the continent — serving Azure, Office 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform from within South Africa. The forward ZAR 5.4bn half of the same announcement is held as 2025-03-06-microsoft-zaf-azure-expansion-2025-microsoft-azure-south-africa-zar-54b.

title: Google — South Africa cloud region (Johannesburg), 2025
description: "Cabinet also welcomed the launch of Google South Africa's R2.5-billion cloud region in Johannesburg, which integrates South Africa into Google Cloud's global network. This project is Google's first in Africa and marks a significant investment in South Africa's technology infrastructure."

title: Vantage Data Centres / Attacq — Johannesburg (Waterfall City) data centre JV, 2025
description: "Real estate developer Attacq and Vantage Data Centres have partnered in a 50:50 joint venture to build a data center in Johannesburg, South Africa. The project forms the first half of Phase II of Vantage's South Africa data center in Waterfall City… The investment for the data center shell is estimated at R628 million ($34m), backed by a 20-year lease. Attacq is expected to partner on the shell only." The JNB1 campus comprises three facilities and will offer 80MW of IT capacity at full buildout; construction underway with completion expected Q1 2026.

title: Absa (syndicated) — Teraco JB7 data centre, 2024
description: Teraco has started building JB7, a 40 MW hyperscale data centre (71,000 m², eight data halls) at its Isando Campus in Ekurhuleni, "funded by a new R8-billion syndicated loan… secured through Absa and other financial institutions to finance JB7 and other construction projects." Part of the loan augments Teraco's renewable-energy programme, including a 120 MW utility-scale solar PV plant wheeling power across the Eskom network.

title: Africa Data Centres South Africa — 20MW Hyperscale Expansion (RMB ZAR2bn Facility, 2024)
description: In June 2024, Africa Data Centres secured a ZAR 2 billion (~US$109.5 million) bespoke financing facility arranged by RMB (Rand Merchant Bank, part of FirstRand Group) to expand hyperscale data centre capacity in South Africa by an additional 20MW. RMB acted as Coordinator, Initial Mandated Lead Arranger, and Bookrunner. The financing enables ADC to accelerate expansion at its existing Midrand (JHB1) and Samrand (JHB2) Johannesburg campuses and Cape Town (CPT1/CPT2) facilities. ADC's South Africa market has capacity of 64MW and the expansion aims to increase this further to serve growing hyperscaler and enterprise demand.

title: US DFC — Africa Data Centres Cape Town (CPT1) expansion, 2024
description: Africa Data Centres, a business of Cassava Technologies, expanded its CPT1 facility in Cape Town by 6 MW of IT load (from 5.5 MW to 11.5 MW), adding 1,000 racks across two colocation halls and one hyperscale hall. The expansion "was implemented through an up to $300 million loan from the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC)."

title: Actis-led consortium acquisition of Swiftnet telecom tower platform from Telkom South Africa
description: Actis, together with Royal Bafokeng Holdings as empowerment partner, acquires 100% of Swiftnet, Telkom South Africa's masts and towers portfolio, at an enterprise value of ZAR 6.75 billion (c. USD 355 million). Actis leads the consortium via Towerco Bidco with a 70% stake; Royal Bafokeng Holdings holds 30%. Swiftnet operates approximately 4,000 towers and masts across South Africa. Transaction completed March 2025 following regulatory approvals from Competition Tribunal (September 2024) and ICASA (December 2024).

title: Too Much Wifi — Debt Investment (Wireless Broadband ISP)
description: BII committed $4.4M to Too Much Wifi (TMWF) in December 2024, a wireless broadband connectivity provider offering uncapped, low-cost, high-speed internet services in South Africa, targeting underserved communities and townships. TMWF provides affordable broadband connectivity to households and small businesses in areas typically excluded from fibre rollout. This investment directly supports digital inclusion and connectivity access.

recipient: Liquid Intelligent Technologies South Africa (Pty) Ltd
title: Liquid Intelligent Technologies Term Loan 2 — South Africa (ZAR)
description: IFC is providing a ZAR-denominated senior term loan of approximately $58.17 million (ZAR equivalent) to Liquid Intelligent Technologies South Africa. This is part of a broader approximately $220 million financing package supporting the continued expansion of Liquid's fibre, broadband, and data centre infrastructure in South Africa. The ZAR denomination reduces currency risk for the company, which generates revenues primarily in local currency.

title: AfricaGrow LP commitment to Knife Capital Fund III
description: AfricaGrow commits to Knife Capital's $50M Series B expansion fund (Knife Fund III) targeting high-growth African technology companies at Series A/B stage. Focus on ICT, fintech, e-commerce, SaaS, healthtech. South Africa-based with pan-African portfolio.

title: DEG Equity Investment in Lulalend (Lula) Digital SME Lender South Africa (2023)
description: DEG participates in the USD 35 million Series B funding round for Lulalend (rebranded Lula), South Africa's leading digital lender providing working capital and financial services to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The round was led by Lightrock with DEG, Triodos Investment Management, Women's World Banking, IFC, and Quona Capital participating. Proceeds service surging demand for fast access to working capital and accelerate the rollout of Lula's digital banking offering for SMEs. The company was launched in 2014 and uses digital technology to assess creditworthiness and disburse loans rapidly.

recipient: Naked Insurance (Naked Financial Technology Pty Ltd)
title: DEG Equity Investment in Naked Insurtech South Africa Series B (2023)
description: DEG participates in the USD 17 million IFC-led equity round for Naked Insurance, South Africa's first fully digital insurance platform. The round is led by IFC with DEG, Hollard, and Yellowwoods as co-investors. Naked uses AI and automation to provide comprehensive and instant vehicle, home, contents, and standalone item insurance. Customers can get a final insurance quote in under 90 seconds and switch or pause cover online. The investment supports Naked's strategy to expand its digital insurance offering to first-time insurance buyers and continue innovation in customer experience. DEG first invested in Naked in 2023; in January 2025 DEG participated in follow-on Series B2 round of USD 38M.

title: UsPlus South Africa — Digital SME Invoice Financing Loan
description: DFC direct loan of $8 million to UsPlus Limited (South Africa), a fintech company providing flexible working capital solutions to small and medium enterprises primarily via digital invoice and purchase order financing. UsPlus uses a digital platform to streamline SME access to working capital in South Africa, addressing the financing gap for underserved businesses.

title: Norrsken22 co-leads TymeBank pre-Series C — South African digital bank
description: Norrsken22 co-leads (with Blue Earth Capital) a $77.8M pre-Series C round for TymeBank, South Africa's leading digital-only challenger bank serving the mass market. TymeBank serves over 9 million customers with zero-fee banking and micro-credit. The round will further expand operations in South Africa and the Philippines. Tencent increases its stake in the round alongside new lead investors Norrsken22 and Blue Earth Capital.

recipient: AWS Africa South Africa cloud infrastructure expansion
title: AWS — South Africa cloud and AI infrastructure, ZAR 30.4bn planned by 2029
description: AWS released a South Africa Economic Impact Study on 13 April 2023 announcing that it plans to invest ZAR 30.4 billion in its cloud infrastructure in South Africa by 2029, covering construction, connection, operation and maintenance of the AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region. The study puts total planned investment at **ZAR 46 billion across 2018–2029**, of which ZAR 15.6 billion had already been spent between 2018 and 2022 (held separately as 2023-04-13-aws-zaf-cape-town-aws-cape-town-region-capex-2018-2022). AWS projects the 2018–2029 investment will contribute an estimated ZAR 80 billion to South African GDP and support an average of more than 5,700 full-time-equivalent jobs annually at local vendors. The AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region launched in April 2020 with three Availability Zones, the first AWS cloud region on the continent. A solar plant in Northern Cape Province generating up to 28,000 MWh a year forms part of the associated renewable-energy programme.

title: Visa South Africa Data Centre and Digital Infrastructure Investment
description: Visa opened its first African data centre in Johannesburg, South Africa in July 2025. The data centre — Visa's fifth globally — is part of a R1 billion (~$54–57 million) investment in South Africa over three years (2023–2025+). It localises processing of South African transactions on VisaNet and forms part of Visa's broader $1 billion Africa digital transformation pledge made in 2022. Investment also covers SME enablement, youth training and merchant digitisation.

title: Fibertime Group South Africa Fibre Internet Expansion
description: Finnfund invested EUR 2 million in Fibertime Group, a South African company providing affordable high-speed fibre internet to underserved township communities. The investment supports Fibertime's goal to connect up to 1.8 million low-income households in South African townships through its fibre and VulaCoin subsidiaries.

title: Liquid ECG Infraco Broadband Loan — South Africa
description: IFC provided a senior loan of approximately $23.89 million to Liquid ECG Infraco (Pty) Ltd, a Liquid Intelligent Technologies subsidiary operating broadband infrastructure in South Africa. The project supports expansion of open-access fibre and broadband connectivity to underserved communities and businesses in South Africa, advancing digital inclusion and supporting the country's digital economy targets.

title: Affordable Off-Grid Connectivity Feasibility Study - South Africa
description: USTDA feasibility study for affordable off-grid internet connectivity in South Africa. Innovative broadband solution for underserved communities.

title: DPI investment in Ukheshe International South Africa digital fintech enabler
description: Development Partners International (DPI), via African Development Partners III (ADP III), co-invests with Fireball Capital in Ukheshe International, a South African digital fintech enablement platform. Ukheshe provides white-label digital financial services infrastructure to banks, telecoms and fintechs including digital wallets, payment APIs, virtual cards, and remittance solutions. Ukheshe subsequently acquired Masterpass (South Africa) in 2022 and EFT Corporation in 2024, expanding its digital payments rails footprint across southern Africa.

title: Equinix Johannesburg JN1 Data Centre — US$160 Million Investment
description: Equinix announced in December 2022 its entry into South Africa with a US$160 million data centre investment in Johannesburg, named JN1. The facility, expected to open mid-2024, represents Equinix's second African country entry following the MainOne acquisition. JN1 provides carrier-neutral colocation and interconnection services in Johannesburg, a major digital hub for southern Africa and gateway to hyperscaler cloud on-ramps. TechCabal (June 2025) reports Equinix has opened its first data centre in Johannesburg.

recipient: Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) / MTN South Africa
title: MTN South Africa 5G/4G Spectrum Acquisition — 2022 ICASA Auction
description: MTN South Africa acquired 100 MHz of high-demand radio frequency spectrum across three bands in the ICASA multi-band spectrum auction concluded 17 March 2022: 2x10MHz in the 800MHz band (R2.9bn / $195.5M), 4x10MHz in the 2600MHz band (R1.1bn / $72.8M), and 4x10MHz in the 3500MHz band (R1.1bn / $75.1M). Total cost: R5.2 billion. This spectrum enables 4G capacity expansion and 5G network rollout across South Africa. R3.3bn was paid to ICASA in April 2022, with the remaining R1.9bn paid in H2 2023 once the 800MHz band was cleared of interference. The auction was South Africa's first spectrum auction in over a decade.

recipient: Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) / Vodacom South Africa
title: Vodacom South Africa 5G/4G Spectrum Acquisition — 2022 ICASA Auction
description: Vodacom South Africa acquired 110 MHz of high-demand radio frequency spectrum in the ICASA multi-band spectrum auction concluded 17 March 2022 — the largest spectrum purchase in the auction. Portfolio: 2x10MHz in the 700MHz band, 80MHz in the 2600MHz band, and 10MHz in the 3500MHz band, for a total of R5.38 billion. The spectrum enables acceleration of 4G coverage and 5G network rollout across South Africa and supports Vodacom's network performance and digital inclusion goals. Spectrum licence effective 1 July 2022 for a 20-year period. R3.2 billion was paid in H1 FY2023 (before July 2022); remaining R2.2 billion paid October 2023 (800MHz band cleared of interference).

title: CPDIF Acquisition of Ctrack Africa and Middle East Operations from Inseego Corp
description: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF) acquired 100% of Ctrack's operations in Africa and the Middle East from Nasdaq-listed Inseego Corp in a transaction valued at approximately ZAR 529 million (~US$36.2 million). This was CPDIF's maiden investment. Ctrack is a leading telematics software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform providing fleet management analytics, insurance risk solutions, and asset tracking solutions across sub-Saharan Africa. Ctrack's IoT and big data analytics platform leverages cloud-based data infrastructure, AI-driven analytics, and IoT connectivity. Headquartered in South Africa. In December 2024, Ctrack additionally acquired Inseego's international telematics business for $52 million.

title: TymeBank / Tyme Group — Equity Investments (Digital Bank)
description: Series of equity investments in TymeBank (Tyme Group Holdings PTE), South Africa's leading digital bank focused on the underbanked. TymeBank integrates physical and digital distribution via kiosks at Pick n Pay and Boxer supermarkets. BII rounds: $18.5M equity (Nov 2021, directly in TymeBank Ltd — subsequently restructured/exited as separate entity), $18.8M equity in Tyme Group Holdings (Sep 2022), $5M equity follow-on (Nov 2022), $2.5M equity (Apr 2023), $1.1M equity (Jul 2024). TymeBank also operates GoTyme in Philippines.

title: Lula Lend Digital SME Lending Platform — South Africa
description: Norfund local currency loan (NOK 110.9 million equivalent, approx USD 10 million per Norfund 2024 statement) to Lula Lend (Lula), a fully digital SME lending fintech in South Africa. Lula uses data-driven credit scoring and digital platforms to provide unsecured working capital loans to SMEs. Digital scope: fully digital lending platform, data-driven underwriting, API-based business banking.

title: Africa Data Centres South Africa — Johannesburg JHB1/JHB2 and Cape Town CPT1/CPT2 Data Centres
description: ADC invested significantly in South Africa as its largest market, operating data centres in Johannesburg (JHB1 Midrand: 14.4MW; JHB2 Samrand: 10MW expanding to 20MW) and Cape Town (CPT1: 12MW expanding to 20MW with new halls; CPT2: 20MW). The first DFC disbursement of $83 million in August 2022 primarily supported South Africa expansion. In June 2024, RMB arranged a ZAR 2 billion (~$109.5 million) bespoke financing facility for ADC to accelerate South Africa hyperscale capacity by an additional 20MW. Combined South Africa capacity from JHB1, JHB2, CPT1, and CPT2 represents 64MW+, the largest ADC market. The July 2024 Cape Town CPT1 expansion added three new halls with 6MW additional IT load.

title: Liquid Telecom South Africa Term Loan
description: IFC provided a $100 million senior term loan to Liquid Telecommunications South Africa (Pty) Ltd, the South African subsidiary of Liquid Intelligent Technologies (formerly Liquid Telecom). The financing supports expansion of fibre optic network capacity and data centre operations across South Africa, enabling affordable broadband for businesses and consumers. South Africa is Liquid's largest single market and home to its Johannesburg-based data centres serving as regional hubs for cloud, colocation, and IP transit services.

description: USTDA feasibility study for Dark Fibre Africa fiber network expansion into peri-urban and rural areas of South Africa. Supports broadband connectivity infrastructure.

title: Western Cape Province Broadband Expansion - South Africa
description: USTDA feasibility study for broadband network expansion in Western Cape Province, South Africa. Supports broadband infrastructure development.

title: Actis acquisition of 85% stake in Octotel fibre network operator South Africa
description: Actis acquires an 85% stake in Octotel, a Cape Town-based fibre-to-the-home (FTTH) network operator focused on the Western Cape, South Africa. Investment of approximately USD 167 million from the Neoma Africa Fund III. Octotel's founders remain as minority shareholders. Strategy focused on expanding homes passed with fibre and driving take-up rates. Actis led a ZAR 2bn social loan facility from RMB in 2022. Actis exited to consortium led by AIIM, STOA and Thebe Investment Corporation in September 2024.

payer: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
title: ICBC contributes to ZAR 2.251 billion syndicated buyer’s credit loan to Telkom SA SOC for the acquisition of Huawei 4G equipment
description: In 2020, Telkom SA SOC Limited signed a ZAR 2.251 billion syndicated buyer’s credit loan agreement with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) and South Africa Standard Bank. The loan carries a 10-year maturity and an unknown interest rate. The borrower also purchased buyer’s credit insurance from Sinosure. The loan proceeds are to be used by the borrower to partially finance a $175 million commercial contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.   The purpose of the project is to acquire and 4G equipment from Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd

recipient: Multiple cloud customers / Huawei Cloud SSA operations
title: Huawei Cloud South Africa — Multi-year cloud infrastructure CapEx (Johannesburg Availability Zones 1–3)
description: Huawei launched its first availability zone (AZ) in South Africa in November 2018/early 2019, becoming the first international cloud service provider with a hyperscale data centre in Africa. Between 2019 and 2022, Huawei Cloud invested more than ZAR 3.5 billion (approximately USD 219 million) in local cloud infrastructure in South Africa, including ultra-large cloud data centres, networks, and services, culminating in the launch of a third AZ in Johannesburg in January 2023. The investment supports IaaS, PaaS and SaaS services for public-sector, financial, telecom, and SME customers across Southern Africa. This is Huawei's own CapEx commitment, not a Chinese state-bank loan; no corresponding china.csv EXIM/CDB loan row covers this investment.

title: TV White Space Wi-Fi Rural Connectivity - South Africa
description: USTDA feasibility study and technical assistance for television white space (TVWS) Wi-Fi rural connectivity in South Africa. Innovative approach to broadband access in underserved areas.

title: AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region — ZAR 15.6bn invested 2018–2022 (disclosed 2023)
description: AWS's South Africa Economic Impact Study, released 13 April 2023, states that AWS invested ZAR 15.6 billion between 2018 and 2022 in the AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region — all cash expenses directly attributable to the region, including imports of specialised equipment and software and in-country spending on construction and data-centre operations. The region launched in April 2020 with three Availability Zones and was the first AWS cloud region on the African continent. AWS puts the GDP contribution of that spend at ZAR 12 billion by end-2022. The forward half of the same study — ZAR 30.4 billion planned by 2029 — is held as 2023-04-13-aws-zaf-cloud-aws-south-africa-cloud-infrastructure-zar-304bn; together they make up the ZAR 46 billion 2018–2029 programme.

title: ICT Investment Analysis - South Africa
description: USTDA ICT investment analysis for South Africa examining ICT sector investment opportunities and market development.

payer: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
title: ICBC provides ZAR 1.3 billion loan to Cell C for second Frame Supply Agreement (FSA2) (Linked to Project ID#58629)
description: On March 30, 2015, Cell C Limited (or “Cell C”), a South African telecommunications company, entered into a second Frame Supply Agreement (FSA2) with Huawei relating to the supply of RAN equipment and the upgrade and expansion of their LTE, MBT, and microwave networks. In the same year, Cell C entered into a Capex loan facility of $240 million and ZAR 1.3 billion with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) to finance this FSA2 (see Project #58629 for the $240 million loan). A 2017 circular to stockholders from Blue Label Telecom (majority stakeholder of Cell C) listed the current value of the loan at R43.051 million (2015: R0 million, 2014: R0 million) with an undrawn facility of R1 256.949 million. The loan bears an interest of JIBAR plus a 3.45% margin, which is accrued monthly and settled quarterly. A percentage of the capital outstanding is repayable annually based on a sliding scale; the balance includes R0.421 million accrued interest. The loan's final  maturity date is June 30, 2023 and it is 50% guaranteed by Oger Telecom Limited.

payer: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
title: ICBC provides $240 million loan to Cell C for second Frame Supply Agreement (FSA2) (Linked to Project ID#58622)
description: On March 30, 2015, Cell C Limited (or “Cell C”), a South African telecommunications company, entered into a second Frame Supply Agreement (FSA2) with Huawei relating to the supply of RAN equipment and the upgrade and expansion of their LTE, MBT, and microwave networks. In the same year, Cell C entered into a Capex loan facility of $240 million and ZAR 1.3 billion with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) to finance this FSA2 (see Project ID#58622 for ZAR portion of financing). According to a 2017 circular to stockholders, Blue Label Telecom (majority stakeholder of Cell C) listed the current value of the loan at $95.473 million (2015: $44.446 million, 2014: $0 million) with an undrawn facility of $144.527 million. The loan bears an interest of Libor + 3.45%, which is accrued monthly and settled quarterly. A percentage of the capital outstanding is repayable annually based on a sliding scale. The balance includes $0.399 million accrued interest, and the loan reaches maturity on 30 June 2023. The loan is 50% guaranteed by Oger Telecom Limited.

title: IHS Fund II SA — OPIC Investment Guaranty
description: OPIC investment guaranty of up to $80 million to IHS Fund II SA PVE, a fund investing in telecommunications tower infrastructure in South Africa. The DFC provided a participating debt commitment of up to $80 million alongside equity from DFIs. IHS Towers is a leading independent tower company in Africa. Investment supports expansion of telecom infrastructure enabling mobile broadband connectivity in South Africa.
